messages:
Sara P.: heads up — customer reported NAT/IP exhaustion in their VPC after we started aggressive control-plane retries during a regional outage. they saw hundreds of ephemeral connections from our agent and hit the provider quota :grimace:
Mike L.: ugh. which flow exactly? control-plane websocket reconnects or agent-side http retries?
Sara P.: websocket reconnects + short-lived grpc retries from the onboarding agent. we retry fast to minimize perceived downtime but it blows up the customer's SNAT table when multiple agents are churned during failover.
Chandra R.: not surprising. retries + many ephemeral source ports = nat table blowout. we’ve seen this in small infra tests too.
Alex G.: quick list of options I can think of: 1) slower backoff on agent reconnects 2) maintain long-lived connection via regional relay 3) preserve source IP using per-tenant ENI / dedicated egress 4) introduce a centralized egress connector that multiplexes traffic
Mike L.: add 5) client-side circuit breaker / token-bucket so agents stop retrying when backend reports overloaded.
Chandra R.: tradeoffs: (1) is simple but increases failover latency. (2) regional relay reduces churn but adds infra and a new failure domain. (3) per-tenant ENI keeps source IP but means extra ENI quotas & cross-account complexity. (4) central connector buys us control but moves cost & state to us.
Sara P.: customer constraint: they cannot add broad peering or allow wildcard source ip ranges. any per-tenant ENI option must run in their account (so they'd need to provision it).
Alex G.: thought: what if we combine token-bucket + sticky egress for a subset of control-plane routes? i.e., keep main reconnects conservative, but for authenticated "heartbeat" channel we try to keep long-lived connection and only fall back to short polling as a last resort.
Mike L.: that splits the problem nicely. keep most traffic low-churn, but we still need a plan for scenarios where long-lived is impossible (corporate proxies, NAT gateways).
Chandra R.: we should also limit the maximum parallel reconnects per VPC. like allow 5 concurrent reconnect attempts per-tenant with exponential backoff and random jitter. that keeps worst-case port usage bounded.
Sara P.: agreed. small config suggestion to prototype: 
```
agent.reconnect:
  max_concurrent_attempts: 5
  base_backoff_ms: 250
  max_backoff_ms: 20000
  jitter: 0.5
  circuit_window_s: 60  # if >50% failures, open circuit for 30s
```
Mike L.: also add server-side 429 telemetry and a per-tenant sliding failure counter we can surface in console so customers know why we're throttling.
Alex G.: for the per-tenant ENI idea — ops impact: requires IaC in customer account, rotation of SG/route tables, and documented hard limits. costlier but deterministic. Should be opt-in enterprise feature.
Chandra R.: central egress connector (us-managed) could preserve IPs but then we have to be careful about cross-account routing and peering NATs. We'd add latency and cost, and need autoscaling to handle multi-tenant spikes.
Sara P.: ok action items: 1) prototype agent-side limits + backoff config and spike test against small customer VPCs — chandra/mike own. 2) add 429 / failure counter telemetry to console — mike. 3) draft an RFC for "IP-preservation opt-in" (per-tenant ENI vs managed egress connector) with cost/ops tradeoffs — alex. 4) communicate interim mitigation to impacted customer: reduce agent parallelism to 2 and enable jitter. — sara will send.
deploy-bot: deployment started for agent v0.42.1 -> canaries (region=us-west-2)
Mike L.: thanks. i'll add the metric hooks before canary finishes.
Chandra R.: i'll run a simulated reconnect storm in a test account post-canary and dump NAT table growth numbers.
Alex G.: RFC ETA: COB next week. i'll include diagrams and cost estimates for 3 deployment models.
Sara P.: perfect. small note: make sure proposed controls are configurable at route level (control plane vs telemetry) so we don't throttle embeddings/hosted inference traffic by accident.
Mike L.: noted. we'll gate on route tag.
Alex G.: and add a follow-up to the runbook: steps to throttle from our side vs customer-side config changes.
Sara P.: thanks team — this thread should be the single source for follow-up. i'll ping in #support when we send the customer mitigation note.
